name: a_strategist_views
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Strategists & positioning.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Named strategist and investor commentary with numbers (index targets, rate calls, sector calls), fund flows, positioning/short-interest data, sentiment gauges, research notes on market-wide themes (AI capex returns, AI productivity surveys, bubble/misallocation debates by named academics or firms).

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Macro / Strategists & Positioning

- **S&P 500:** Panmure Liberum analyst Joachim Klement forecast the index at **5,000 by end-2027**, citing higher bond yields and interest rates as risks to the equity bull market; the call was published Monday, October 5, 2026, before the 12:20 ET cutoff. (Reuters, Oct. 5, 2026, 04:30 ET)

- **U.S. 10-year Treasury:** The benchmark yield reached **5.34%** on Thursday, October 1, its highest level in **24 years**, according to Reuters’ weekend market report. (Reuters, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **U.S. 10-year Treasury:** Chris Galipeau, head market strategist at the Franklin Templeton Institute, said a move to **6%** would materially change the market discussion; the yield was approximately **5.3%** in the report. (Moneycontrol, Oct. 4, 2026, 09:49 ET)

- **Equity outlook:** Tracie McMillion, head of global asset allocation strategy at Wells Fargo Investment Institute, said seasonal strength in the fourth quarter faced headwinds from higher yields and other macro risks. (Reuters, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Rates and equities:** Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer of Horizon Investment Services, called interest rates the market’s “biggest headwind” and said a meaningful equity rally would be difficult without relief in rates. (Reuters, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **AI capex:** Nelson Yu, head of equities at AllianceBernstein, identified hyperscaler **capital-expenditure revisions** as the “number one” item to monitor during third-quarter earnings. (Reuters, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Market breadth and AI concentration:** Kevin Gordon, head of macro research and strategy at Charles Schwab, said the S&P 500 was approximately **1% below its high** while the average stock had experienced a **14% drawdown**; he said AI-related technology stocks were supporting the index and that one major-capital-spending shortfall could disrupt the market. (Bloomberg, Oct. 5, 2026, 07:22 ET)

- **Seasonality:** Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA, said fourth quarters of midterm years had historically produced an average **6.4% gain** for stocks. (Reuters, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Long-term seasonality:** CFRA data cited in a weekend market report showed the S&P 500 had averaged a **4.2% fourth-quarter gain since 1945** and had risen in **85%** of fourth quarters. (Reuters, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Market outlook:** Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth, said higher energy prices and Treasury yields had kept investors on the sidelines during the prior month; he also identified narrow AI-related leadership as a question for October. (CNBC, Oct. 2, 2026, 14:35 ET)

- **Rates and portfolio allocation:** JPMorgan Asset Management reported that the U.S. 10-year yield reached **5.2%** in late September, more than **100 basis points** above its level at the start of 2026; the firm highlighted short-duration government bonds, high-yield credit, and equities outside U.S. technology as areas of focus. (J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Oct. 2, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Yield curve:** JPMorgan Asset Management reported that September 2026 Treasury yields rose **53 basis points to 5.27%** at the two-year maturity and **38 basis points to 5.62%** at the 30-year maturity. (J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Oct. 2, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Rate-hike probability:** JPMorgan Asset Management said the Overnight Index Swap market priced a **37% implied probability** of a rate hike at the October Federal Open Market Committee meeting. (J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Oct. 2, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Equity and Treasury returns:** JPMorgan Asset Management reported that the S&P 500 fell **0.3%** in September while the Nasdaq rose **1.9%**, during a month in which the 10-year Treasury yield rose **40 basis points**. (J.P. Morgan Asset Management, Oct. 2, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Earnings and AI spending:** Bloomberg Intelligence estimated that third-quarter technology-sector EPS would rise by more than **65%** year over year, compared with projected S&P 500 EPS growth of more than **24%**; Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta were reported to have negative annual free cash flow amid AI infrastructure spending. (Moneycontrol, Oct. 4, 2026, 09:49 ET)

- **Equity valuation risk:** Fundstrat economic strategist Hardika Singh estimated that equity valuations historically begin compressing when the 10-year Treasury yield exceeds approximately **5.5%**; the yield was reported at approximately **5.28%** at the end of the week. (The Wealth Advisor, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)

- **Earnings outlook:** UBS projected S&P 500 profits to grow **25% in 2026** and another **14% in 2027**, according to a weekend market report. (The Wealth Advisor, Oct. 4, 2026, publication time not available)
